minutes.headline: Task force backed a Hanford styrofoam recycling drop-off, and voted to ask the select board to swap associate members for alternates.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force heard an update on a styrofoam recycling pilot at Hanford, with open questions on bags, grants and what is accepted. It discussed a March technical assistance grant, a plan to consult the state adviser Kelly, and how to keep meetings and agendas regular. It voted to authorize the chair to ask the select board to change two associate seats to alternates, to bring Tyler on, and set the next meeting for March 3 at six by Zoom.

public_comment.topic: A former taxpayer and still registered voter reminded everyone of spring election season, two open select board seats, and the mid-March citizens caucus as the easy route onto the ballot.

votes.motion: Approve the prior meeting minutes (roll call)
Authorize the chair to ask the select board to convert the two associate members to alternate members and start the process to get Tyler onto the committee
votes.outcome: passed unanimously by roll call; chair declared the ayes have it

budget_items.what_was_said: The recycler would charge a fee per pickup to recycle a container held at Hanford.
The container cost is still to be determined, and Tyler is to look for a grant to offset it.
Members discussed a token charge per bag to help fund the system, and keeping it at or below the cost of normal trash bags.
Kim gave the price of the large Lunenburg trash bags as a comparison unit.
If bag revenue exceeds the pickup fee, the container cost could be offset over some number of loads.
A local sponsor or investor might fund the one-time container purchase.
The committee is awaiting word on the grant it applied for, expected around end of February or early March.
A state technical assistance award is available to help identify programs for the next round of grant funding, with an application deadline in March.
Money placed in the earlier budget for grant writing has not been used, and the interim town manager suggested a better use. A full-time grant writer was described as likely to pay for themselves.
Dave described last year's override impact on an average home and how it scales per million, and said capital work has been backed up for years.

what_happened.line: The task force voted unanimously by roll call to authorize the chair to ask the select board to convert two associate seats to alternates and start the process to add Tyler.
Members heard a pilot plan for a styrofoam recycling drop-off at Hanford; the container cost and a per-bag charge are undecided, and Tyler is to look for a grant.
The committee is awaiting word on its fall Green Communities grant, and a state technical assistance application is due in March; the chair will consult the state adviser Kelly first.
Members discussed unused grant-writing money and the tax impact of building projects; no resolution was reached.
The next meeting was set for the first Monday in March, the third, at six o'clock by Zoom.

why_it_matters: The styrofoam drop-off would be paid for partly by a per-bag charge on residents, so the container cost, any grant and the price per bag decide what a household would pay to use it.
The seat change goes to the select board, which decides who may sit on the committee and vote, and the fall grant decision bears on what the town can fund in energy work, including at a school.
